latest_release.name: 2.1.50 Move chats between projects, and chats that keep going
latest_release.body:
## 2.1.50 Move chats between projects, and chats that keep going

You can now move a chat into another project by dragging it or from its menu, with Undo. Long chats keep going in more situations: when a step is not picked up, the app keeps trying, tells you, and lets you continue with one click. The browser extension now updates itself even while long chats run, and very long chats no longer slow the app down.

### 👉 After updating

- Nothing to do. The browser extension updates itself. A chat that is still answering delays that by at most 30 minutes; a tool call or a message being sent still finishes first.

### ✨ New

- **Move chats between projects.** Drag a chat onto a project, or onto one of its groups, or use **Move to project** in the chat's menu. A notice says where it went and offers **Undo**. Chat lists also show **Today**, **Yesterday** and earlier date headings. The move happens only in the app; a chat linked to a ChatGPT Project stays where it is in ChatGPT.
- **The new project's folder, said once.** After you move a chat into a project, your next message there tells ChatGPT the project's folder once, so it works in the right place.
- **Continue now and Try now.** When a chat's quick tries run out, the app tells you, also on your phone if you set that up, and the chat's notice has **Continue now** or **Try now** to go on at once.
- **Continue from the last summary.** When ChatGPT stops serving a chat for good, the app can continue it in a new ChatGPT chat from its last summary, still as one chat in the app.

### 💪 Better

- **Chats keep going.** After its quick tries, the app no longer gives up on a step that nobody picked up. It keeps trying every 15 to 60 minutes and says why a step waits. An automatic Continue that waited too long is sent as an ordinary message.
- **Fresh turns by default.** When ChatGPT shows only Stop for a long time, the app stops and continues in a fresh turn. This was an experimental option and is now on for everyone; you can still turn it off in Settings.
- **The extension updates during long runs.** It used to wait until no chat was answering, which in busy setups could mean never.
- **Big chats stay fast.** In very long chats, the app no longer reads the whole history again and again. An automatic Continue that no longer fits the chat's last question is withdrawn instead of being offered for hours.
- **Thorough Goal helpers get time.** A Goal or Loop helper set to extra-high or Pro reasoning now gets up to 12 or 20 minutes for its next message instead of timing out after three.
- **Workers in the right mode.** A worker chat picks its own model before its wake-up message is typed.
- **Compact chat lists.** Rows in Projects and Chats are tighter, so more chats fit on screen, and the keyboard focus outline is fully visible again. Inbox cards stay as they were.
- **Chat menus on short windows.** A chat's menu that fit on neither side of its button showed a scrollbar for a few pixels. It now opens whole beside the button.
- **Plugins, Skills and Pets** say when their list could not be loaded, instead of "Loading…" for good.
- **Layout polish:** the + menu, text fields in Settings and the update card in every language.

### 🛠 Fixed

- **Loop chats that stopped when the helper's message got too long.** The helper was never told the length limit, so in long Loop chats its messages grew until one no longer fit, and every retry failed the same way. It is now told the limit, and after a message that was too long it is asked for a shorter one.
- **The composer gear was missing on an empty message box.** After a change on ChatGPT's side, the Chat On Steroids gear only appeared once you typed something. It is back on every composer.
- **Recovery that stopped while a tab was stuck.** A tab stuck in rendering mode could stop the app from recovering any chat. Recovery now goes on, and a chat that needs its tab shown gets it shown once.

## What you get
### When it needs a human, it says so Some steps only you can do: a sign-in, a USB key, a command it must not run. ChatGPT hands you a **step for you**, with the exact command, the folder and what it expects to see. You run it yourself and mark it **done**; the app never runs it. ### Know what your chats are doing, away from your desk Get a message when a chat finishes, needs you or fails, through the free **ntfy** app or a **Telegram bot of your own**. With Telegram you can also ask `/status`, stop or pause a chat, and deny an approval from your phone. Nothing can be allowed remotely.
### When a chat is stuck, one row tells you why Since when, how often the app tried, and every step it took. It turns amber once the app has stopped trying, so you know when it needs you. ### Give a project more context, not more access Add related folders to a project so ChatGPT knows about them. They never become the working folder and never widen what it may touch.
### Link your own Telegram bot in a minute Create a bot with @BotFather, paste its token, and send the shown code to it. Notifications then also arrive in Telegram. ntfy keeps working until you turn its switch off in the phone notification settings, and with "Include chat names and answers" on, either one can carry chat names and answers. ### Keep chats in projects Move a chat into a project from its menu or by dragging it, and undo it right away. Chats are grouped by date, and a project's folder is where its chats work.
- **Pick the model and effort per chat**, with the same controls ChatGPT offers. - **Folders you control.** Choose exactly which folders ChatGPT may touch, and what it may do there. - **Limit how many chats work at once**, so a busy day does not hit your usage in one burst. - **Command output in a dock.** Watch what a running command prints, read-only, and stop it with one click. - **Skills, plugins and pets**, 13 languages, light and dark.

## Responsible use and provider rules Chat On Steroids is an independent, open-source workspace for coding and other authorized tasks with your own files and tools. It is intended to support productive work within the rules of the services you use. **It is not intended to bypass usage limits, account restrictions or safety controls.** Use CoS in accordance with OpenAI's applicable [Terms of Use](https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/) ([Europe Terms](https://openai.com/policies/eu-terms-of-use/) for the EEA, Switzerland and UK), [Usage Policies](https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies/) and [Service Terms](https://openai.com/policies/service-terms/), plus your workspace's rules and any connected service's terms. - **Respect limits and access decisions.** Workers, Goal/Loop, Compact & Resume and finish checkpoints organize work; they do not grant extra quota or model access and must not be used to evade rate limits, usage caps or account restrictions. Do not switch accounts, chats, plugins or tunnels to evade a restriction. - **Respect safety decisions.** Do not use local tools, browser control, plugins or another worker to carry out an action that the provider blocked for safety. A local permission or an enabled MCP plugin is not permission to override a provider refusal. - **Understand the integration.** CoS connects local tools through MCP. Its browser extension also observes and automates the ChatGPT browser UI and records conversation content locally. This browser integration is not a public ChatGPT automation API. MCP availability does not establish permission for every form of browser automation or recording; OpenAI's terms also restrict automated or programmatic extraction of data or output. - **Use at your own risk.** Review the rules for your account and intended workflow before connecting, supervise automation and review tool actions and outputs. CoS cannot guarantee policy compliance, continued service access or protection from account warnings, restrictions or suspension. If a workflow is restricted or receives a policy warning, stop that workflow and seek clarification through the provider's support or appeal process. This notice states the project's intended use; it does not certify compliance or change provider rules. CoS is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by OpenAI. The software is provided as-is under the [MIT license](LICENSE); applicable statutory rights remain unaffected. See [Security](SECURITY.md) for local permissions and risks.
## Get started 1. **Install CoS** and open **Settings → Setup**. It walks you through seven short steps, with pictures of what to click. 2. **Connect your browser** (step 1): load the browser extension in Chrome, Edge or Brave. Setup shows your browser's own extensions page in your language: turn on **Developer mode**, click **Load unpacked** and choose the folder that **Open extension folder** shows. Pairing is automatic. 3. **Share a folder and choose access** (steps 2–3): the folder ChatGPT may work in, and what it may do there. 4. **Connect Core** (steps 4–7): create a tunnel and a restricted API key at OpenAI, press **Connect**, then add the app in ChatGPT under **Plugins → Add → Add custom MCP server**. [Tunnel setup →](docs/setup.md#tunnel-setup) 5. **Choose a model, write your task and send.**
Requirements & installation notes Windows 10/11, **macOS 13 Ventura or newer**, or a current desktop Linux. Chrome 125+, current Edge or Brave, plus a ChatGPT account/workspace that can create custom MCP apps (availability depends on your plan and workspace policy). [Check account availability](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt). - **Unsigned beta:** Windows is not publisher-signed; macOS is unsigned and unnotarized. Verify the package against the release checksums. Because of that, macOS asks once after each update for your login password so the new version can open its saved keys ("chat-on-steroids Safe Storage"); choose **Always Allow**. Until you answer, chats and the browser connection wait, and the app says so. - **Linux:** a Secret Service keyring is required. Prefer the DEB; when unprivileged user namespaces are disabled, the AppImage launcher can fall back to --no-sandbox. - **Permissions:** choose your approved folders and review capabilities before connecting. Fresh installs enable Core capabilities and two workers; Windows also enables Desktop permissions. Shell commands run with your normal user privileges. - **Languages:** English, German, Spanish, French, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Japanese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. Choose one in **Appearance → Language**. - **After updating:** the browser extension updates itself once no chat is busy. If CoS asks you to refresh its apps in ChatGPT, do so; **Automatic plugin refresh** in Settings can do it for you.
